We need to create ExecutionContext with ExecutionConfig set appropriately. ExecutionConfig class not shown, but we can use ExecutionContext's default constructor which creates ExecutionConfig with default settings (likely failFast false). To set failFast true, we need to construct ExecutionConfig with failFast true, or use setter on ExecutionContext? There's method executionContext.setFailFast(boolean) maybe? In the code earlier they used executionContext.setFailFast(false). So ExecutionContext has setFailFast method. Let's assume it exists.

Thus test: create ExecutionContext ec = new ExecutionContext(); ec.setFailFast(true); instantiate OneOfValidator (needs many parameters). But reportChildErrors is protected, so we need to access via subclass or reflection. Since test class is in same package com.networknt.schema, protected method is accessible to subclass or same package? Protected allows access within same package. The test class is in same package, so we can call oneOfValidator.reportChildErrors(ec) directly.

We need to construct OneOfValidator. It requires SchemaLocation, JsonNodePath, JsonNode schemaNode, JsonSchema parentSchema, ValidationContext validationContext. We can mock many of these using Mockito, because we only need to call reportChildErrors which doesn't use internal fields. So we can pass null for schemaNode? The constructor checks schemaNode.isArray() and throws if not array. So we need a schemaNode that is an array node. We can create a JsonNode using Jackson's JsonNodeFactory or ObjectMapper. For simplicity, we can mock JsonNode and stub isArray() true. Also validationContext needed, but not used in method. So we can mock ValidationContext.

Thus in @BeforeEach we set up mocks and instantiate OneOfValidator.
